content: The high costs associated with diabetes medications, particularly insulin, create a substantial obstacle for numerous patients, often hindering their ability to follow prescribed treatment regimens. This financial burden frequently forces patients to ration their insulin, miss doses, or forgo other critical diabetes-related healthcare services. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) underscores the importance of healthcare providers actively assessing patients for financial difficulties and identifying cost-related obstacles to accessing necessary medications. Addressing and mitigating these financial barriers can lead to improved physical health outcomes, better psychological well-being, and an overall enhancement in the quality of life for individuals living with diabetes.
